title: Pilot Plan (Draft) — Air-gapped installs w/ signed offline bundles (Redwood Private)
content:
Doc purpose
This is a working pilot plan for validating signed offline bundles + offline verification flows for Redwood Private air-gapped installs. Audience: Private Deployments Eng + Security + SE/CS + Support. This is not customer-facing.

Background / why this pilot
Regulated/on-prem customers are increasingly requiring:
- Artifact integrity guarantees for media transfer (USB / offline repo) and full offline verification (no outbound calls).
- Auditable provenance and predictable behavior (fail-closed; break-glass only with explicit acknowledgement + audit trail).

Pilot objectives (what we are proving)
1) Technical: Customer can install Redwood Private from an offline bundle in an air-gapped network using our installer verification steps (signature + checksums) and succeed on first or second attempt with clear remediations.
2) Security/compliance: Verification is fail-closed by default; break-glass override is both hard to use accidentally and generates unambiguous audit evidence.
3) Operational: Support can diagnose verification/install failures using a standard diagnostics bundle and a repeatable escalation path.
4) Product: Bundle format and docs are understandable enough that a customer security team can approve the approach without bespoke engineering.

In-scope pilot features
- Offline bundle format (v1): bundle manifest, per-artifact digests, bundle-level signature envelope.
- Installer verification UX (pre-unpack or pre-install; exact gate depends on final flow):
  - “verify-only” command
  - verification integrated into install path (fail-closed)
  - break-glass override flow w/ explicit acknowledgement prompt
- Offline provenance references (commit SHA, build id) surfaced in logs/manifest for audit/export.

Out of scope for this pilot
- Customer-managed signing (customer provides keys and signs Redwood artifacts).
- Multi-key trust stores with complex enterprise PKI integration beyond our published public key + key rotation policy.
- Migrating all existing distribution mechanisms; this pilot is exclusively the offline/air-gapped bundle path.

Pilot success criteria (exit gates)
A. Install + verify success
- 2 pilot customers complete: (1) verify bundle offline, (2) install, (3) validate core services healthy.
- 0 cases where the installer proceeds with a failed verification unless break-glass is explicitly invoked.
- Verification completes in < 2 minutes on typical customer hardware (goal; we will record actuals).

B. Failure modes are diagnosable
- For each induced failure class below, the installer returns a distinct exit code + actionable message:
  1) Corrupted bundle file / partial copy
  2) Manifest mismatch (digest mismatch)
  3) Signature invalid / wrong key
  4) Unsupported schema version / downgrade attempt
  5) Missing artifacts
- Support can resolve/triage within 1 business day using standard logs/diagnostics.

C. Security evidence / auditability
- Audit log record produced for:
  - verify success
  - verify failure
  - break-glass override attempt + completion (including provided acknowledgement text)
- Bundle metadata includes release version + commit SHA(s) + build id, and can be attached to customer change tickets.

D. Customer experience
- Customer security team accepts signing/verification explanation + key custody/rotation story without requiring custom changes.
- Docs feedback results in a concrete list of changes and at least 1 revised draft.

Candidate pilot customers (draft; subject to GTM + Security approval)
We should target customers with real air-gap constraints and motivated internal champions. This is not a sales pipeline doc; keep details light.

Pilot candidate A: Northbridge Defense Systems (regulated/defense)
- Deployment: strict air-gap, removable media transfer, internal change board.
- Key requirement themes from discovery: no outbound calls, explicit integrity verification, audit evidence suitable for external review.
- Why good pilot: strong “real world” constraints; will stress docs and verification UX.
- Risks: lengthy approval cycles; may require additional evidence artifacts; change windows limited.

Pilot candidate B: “Rivermark Financial Services” (placeholder until confirmed)
- Deployment: offline staging environment, heavily controlled outbound access.
- Why good pilot: high operational maturity; can provide detailed feedback on runbooks + day-2 ops.
- Risks: will ask about key rotation and long-term verifiability of old bundles.

Pilot candidate C (backup): “Helios Health Research Network” (placeholder until confirmed)
- Deployment: partially disconnected environment (no public internet; internal artifact mirrors allowed).
- Why backup: still exercises offline verification and supply-chain concerns; shorter cycle time.

NOTE: Final customer selection to be confirmed with Product (Vivek/Naomi), SE leadership, and Security (Marcus) after Phase 2 readiness review.

Pilot timeline (target)
- Week 0: internal readiness review + lab rehearsal (air-gapped simulation)
- Week 1: customer onboarding call + security review package share
- Week 2: bundle delivery via agreed transfer method + offline verification dry run
- Week 3: install window + validation + first feedback pass
- Week 4: follow-up, doc updates, closeout report, and go/no-go for expanding pilot

Rollout plan (detailed steps)
0) Internal prerequisites (must be complete before any customer gets artifacts)
- Bundle build output reproducible for the pilot release candidate (RC).
- Signing stage enabled in release pipeline for pilot artifacts (no manual local signing).
- Public verification key distribution mechanism defined (what key, where it’s published, and how it’s versioned).
- Installer has:
  - verify command
  - install gating with fail-closed
  - break-glass behavior requiring explicit acknowledgement
  - structured logs for verification outcome
- Support diagnostics bundle includes verification logs + manifest metadata snapshot.

1) Pilot readiness review (30–45 min, internal)
Attendees: Markus (SE), Fatima (SME), Ethan (installer), Connor (release eng), Marcus (security), Dev Patel (support), Rachel (CS).
Checklist:
- Threat model assumptions reviewed and approved for pilot.
- Break-glass policy confirmed (when allowed, who approves, how logged).
- Known limitations documented and communicated (e.g., no customer-managed keys).
- “Known-good” RC bundle validated in lab.
- Customer-facing docs draft reviewed by Kira/Elliot and Security.

2) Customer onboarding
- Create customer-specific pilot Slack channel (internal only) and external comms plan (email + shared doc).
- Establish roles:
  - Customer technical owner (IT/infra)
  - Customer security approver
  - Redwood SE lead (Markus or delegate)
  - Redwood on-call contact for install window
- Share pilot package:
  - Installation + verification guide (draft)
  - Key rotation + trust model FAQ (draft)
  - Support data we will request in case of failure (log bundle)
- Confirm transfer method details:
  - USB drive / offline NAS / internal repo import
  - expected checksum method for large file copies (we should recommend a pre-verify checksum step)

3) Bundle delivery + offline verify dry run
- Provide offline bundle + detached signature(s) + published public key (or certificate chain, if we go that route).
- Customer performs:
  - file copy into air-gapped environment
  - verify-only command
- Capture metrics:
  - verify duration
  - any errors/warnings
  - customer questions about key trust / provenance

4) Install window
- Pre-flight:
  - confirm target cluster meets prerequisites
  - confirm time sync expectations (if relevant) and document if installer depends on system clock for any checks
  - confirm storage capacity (bundles can be large)
- Execute installation with verification enabled (default path).
- Validate:
  - control plane up
  - core services healthy
  - basic inference request from inside customer network (if allowed)
- Export evidence:
  - verification success log entry
  - manifest metadata recorded in customer change ticket (if they want)

5) Upgrade/rollback exercise (if customer allows within pilot window)
- Run “upgrade from signed offline bundle” once to validate mechanics.
- If upgrade not possible, simulate a rollback scenario in lab and document in closeout.

6) Closeout + feedback capture
- Schedule a 45-minute retrospective with customer stakeholders.
- Collect:
  - docs feedback
  - pain points in verification UX
  - gaps in security evidence
  - operational concerns (rotation, long-term verification, incident response expectations)
- Deliver internal closeout memo:
  - what worked
  - what broke
  - severity and frequency
  - prioritized backlog items (docs + engineering)

Support coverage plan
Pilot installs are “high-touch.” We should explicitly staff coverage around customer install windows.

Coverage model
- Primary: Markus Klein (SE) for customer comms + live troubleshooting coordination.
- Secondary (engineering): Ethan Park (installer) during install window; Connor O’Brien (release/signing) for artifact issues.
- Security escalation: Marcus Lin (design/security review) and Fiona McCarthy (incident/IR guidance if key integrity concerns arise).
- Support: Dev Patel as support liaison; ensure tickets route to a defined queue with internal runbook link.

Support hours / SLAs (pilot)
- For scheduled install windows: live coverage during window + 2 hours post-window.
- For verification failures outside window: next-business-day response, unless customer is in an active change window.

Triage categories (what to do first)
1) “Verification fails immediately”
- Collect: installer version, bundle version, verification exit code, verification log snippet, manifest, signature file, and hash of top-level bundle file.
- Most likely causes: partial/corrupted transfer, wrong signature/public key, schema mismatch.

2) “Verification passes but install fails later”
- Collect: full installer logs + component logs; this is not a signing problem (but we still record provenance fields).

3) “Customer requests break-glass override”
- Require: explicit justification + approval path per policy.
- Ensure: audit log includes acknowledgement text; attach to support case.

Feedback capture plan (how we avoid losing learnings)
- Single running “pilot issues” log (internal) with: date, customer, severity, summary, suspected cause, owner, status.
- After each customer session, SE posts a short summary to internal thread with:
  - what changed
  - logs attached location
  - open questions
- Record doc edits requested by customers as concrete PR/doc tasks (ENG-3918 or docs PR).
- Weekly internal checkpoint (15 min) during pilot month.

Key risks + mitigations
Risk: Digest mismatch after media transfer (common)
- Mitigation: Recommend customer performs a pre-verify of the bundle file hash after transfer; add doc callout “most common failure.” Ensure error text suggests re-copying and checking filesystem integrity.

Risk: Customers question trust distribution (how do they know the public key is legit?)
- Mitigation: Provide a clear key distribution story (where key is published, how it’s pinned, how rotations are communicated). Consider publishing key fingerprint in multiple channels (docs + release notes).

Risk: Break-glass is overused or confusing
- Mitigation: Make break-glass hard to invoke; ensure acknowledgement text is explicit; ensure docs clearly state this is exceptional and logged.

Risk: Slow verification on large bundles
- Mitigation: Benchmark verify path; consider parallel hashing; ensure progress messages if >30s.

Risk: Downgrade/replay confusion (older bundles)
- Mitigation: Document supported versions; add installer checks for minimum allowed versions if policy requires.

Pilot readiness artifacts (what we should have ready to share)
- Customer install + verify guide (draft)
- FAQ: key custody, rotation cadence, how old bundles remain verifiable, what happens on key compromise
- Troubleshooting checklist + diagnostics bundle instructions
- One-page threat model summary (sanitized)

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm final candidate customers with GTM + Product (names above include placeholders).
- Confirm whether we will ship the public key as:
  - embedded in installer,
  - shipped alongside bundle,
  - or published to a pinned URL (note: must support fully offline verification).
- Decide whether we require customers to import the public key into a local trust store vs passing a file path.
- Clarify what exact evidence we can export without leaking sensitive environment info (Kevin to advise).
- Determine whether we will run an upgrade exercise in both pilots or only one.

Owners (initial)
- Pilot coordination + customer comms: Markus Klein
- Air-gap constraints / environment validation: Fatima Noor
- Installer verification flow + UX: Ethan Park (+ Benji Okafor for policy integration)
- Signing pipeline + artifact publishing: Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer, Devon Price
- Security review + break-glass policy: Marcus Lin, Naomi Feldman
- Audit evidence/logging/export: Kevin Osei
- Support readiness + runbook adoption: Dev Patel, Rachel Kim

Notes
- Keep all pilot artifacts (bundles, signatures, keys) clearly labeled “PILOT/RC” to avoid cross-contamination with GA releases.
- We should run at least one full end-to-end rehearsal in the lab that mimics customer transfer (copy to external drive, unplug network, verify, install) before shipping anything to a customer.
